message.content:
In /bench/repo (Go project, memos fork), answer with evidence:

(1) Among functions/methods DECLARED under /bench/repo/internal/, which single one has the highest inbound-call count (fan-in) across the whole repo (non-test and test both countable, but note the split)? Approach: list the packages under internal/ (util, base, version, markdown, webhook, cache, etc.), identify heavily-used helpers (e.g. util.UUID/GenUUID, base validation helpers, version.GetCurrentVersion, markdown render helpers), then grep call sites, e.g. `grep -rn "util\.<Name>(" --include=*.go` and count. Check several candidates and report the winner with symbol, declaration path:line, and approximate caller count. Also report the runner-up.

(2) In the data layer (store/ package: types like Memo, User, Attachment, Reaction, Inbox, IdentityProvider defined in store/*.go), which entity type is referenced from the largest number of DISTINCT Go packages outside store/ (i.e. references to `store.Memo`, `store.User`, etc. in server/, cmd/, internal/, store subpackages count as outside the root store package? — count packages outside the store root, note whether you include store/db subpackages)? Rank top two with rough package counts. Use grep like `grep -rln "store\.User\b" --include=*.go` and count distinct directories.

Return concise findings with paths.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
Findings.

## (1) Highest fan-in function declared under `internal/`

**Winner: `(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement`**
- Declared: `/bench/repo/internal/filter/engine.go:74`
- **~38 call sites** total: **31 in tests**, **7 non-test**.
  - Tests (all in-package): `/bench/repo/internal/filter/functions_test.go` (17), `engine_test.go` (8), `time_test.go` (6)
  - Non-test: `/bench/repo/internal/filter/helpers.go:11`, `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo_relation.go:87,98`, `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go:85`, `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/memo_relation.go:78`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:413`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:356`
- It is also the most *widely distributed* internal symbol (6 distinct packages call it), unlike the runner-up.

**Runner-up: `filter.NewEngine`** — `/bench/repo/internal/filter/engine.go:24`, **32 call sites** (30 test, 2 non-test — both inside `engine.go` in `DefaultEngine`/`DefaultAttachmentEngine`). Essentially test-only fan-in.

Next tier (for calibration):
- `filter.NewSchema` — `/bench/repo/internal/filter/schema.go:89` — 29 calls (28 test)
- `(*renderer).addArg` / `addBoolArg` — `/bench/repo/internal/filter/render.go:842,851` — 29 calls, all inside `render.go` (package-internal, zero external fan-in)
- `util.GenUUID` — `/bench/repo/internal/util/util.go:40` — **28 calls: 21 test / 7 non-test**, spread over 6 non-test files (`server/auth/token.go:194`, `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go:26,135`, `attachment_service_storage.go:209`, `user_service_access_tokens.go:84`, `sso_username.go:15`, `shortcut_service.go:154`). The 21 test hits are heavily concentrated in one file (`server/router/api/v1/test/auth_test.go`, 19).

Other candidates checked and eliminated: `util.ConvertStringToInt32` (5), `util.HasPrefixes`/`ValidateEmail`/`ReplaceString` (0), `version.GetCurrentVersion` (3), `version.IsVersionGreaterThan` (4), all `markdown.Service` methods (≤5), `webhook.ValidateURL` (3), `scheduler.New` (12, but only in `doc.go` comments + in-package example/integration tests), `base` (only the `UIDMatcher` var, 8 uses, no funcs declared).

Caveat: counts are grep-based occurrence counts of `name(`, disambiguated by declaration lookup; ambiguous names (`Error`, `New`, `Len`, `Next`, `Parse`, `Compile`, `Validate`, `Info`, `Transcribe`, `NewClient`, `Register`) were individually resolved and none of the internal-declared ones exceeds ~20 genuine calls.

## (2) Store entity referenced from the most distinct packages

Counting distinct directories (= packages) containing `store.<Type>` references. Root `store` package files use the types unqualified, so they never appear; the counts below therefore include `store/db/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}` and `store/test`, which are separate packages from the `store` root.

**#1 `store.User`** (`/bench/repo/store/user.go:29`) — **11 distinct packages**, 128 raw references:
`server/router/api/v1` (19 files), `server/router/api/v1/test` (3), `server/router/rss` (2), `server/router/fileserver` (2), `server/auth` (2), `server/router/frontend` (1), `server/notification` (1), `store/test` (3), `store/db/sqlite`, `store/db/postgres`, `store/db/mysql`.

**#2 `store.Memo`** (`/bench/repo/store/memo.go:35`) — **10 distinct packages**, 162 raw references (highest raw count, but one fewer package):
`server/router/api/v1` (13), `store/test` (7), `server/router/api/v1/test` (3), `server/router/rss` (2), `server/runner/memopayload`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/notification`, `store/db/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}`.

If you **exclude** the `store/` subtree entirely, the ranking is unchanged but tighter: `store.User` = 7 packages, `store.Memo` = 6.

Others: `store.Attachment` (`store/attachment.go:16`) 8 pkgs / 100 refs; `store.Inbox` (`store/inbox.go:24`) 7 / 61; `store.MemoRelation` 7 / 57; `store.Reaction` (`store/reaction.go:7`) 6 / 43; `store.IdentityProvider` (`store/idp.go:12`) 4 / 30; `store.UserSetting` 4 / 27.

Note: `cmd/memos/main.go` is the only file under `cmd/` or `internal/` touching `store.` at all, and it references only the `store.Store` constructor path — no entity types, so neither `cmd` nor any `internal` package contributes to the counts above.
